speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any changes in your urination, such as urgency, frequency, or blood in the urine?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; the persistence of fever and flank pain despite treated sinusitis suggests a possible spread of infection to the kidneys. Did you experience any burning during urination or see any blood in your urine recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: The new rash after amoxicillin but resolving with cephalexin suggests a specific medication allergy, but I need to clarify the flank pain details. Did you notice any tenderness when tapping on your side, or have you passed any kidney stones? Also, please estimate how much urine you have passed in the last 24 hours and if it looks cloudy. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Leukocyturia: Present, Bacterial_Culture: Negative, Cytospin_Stained_With_Hansel’s_Solution: 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm

speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis shows white blood cells in the urine, yet the bacterial culture is negative. Combined with the eosinophilic cells found in the cytospin, this suggests an allergic interstitial nephritis rather than a typical bacterial infection. Did you notice any recent skin rashes, joint pain, or a generalized body ache in addition to your fever and flank pain?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: No nausea or vomiting is noted, which helps rule out severe sepsis. Given the eosinophilic cells on cytospin and your history of developing a rash with amoxicillin, do you recall if you took any other new medications or supplements in the past few weeks? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count

speaker: Doctor
text: I have reviewed your Complete Blood Count results, which show normal readings, further supporting that this is not a typical bacterial infection or severe systemic reaction. To confirm the diagnosis of allergic interstitial nephritis, I need to see the current kidney imaging. REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: The sinus symptoms improved, but the flank pain and fever stayed. The rash happened during the antibiotics and then resolved after the change in medication.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Allergic Interstitial Nephritis (AIN) secondary to antibiotic exposure. The clinical picture of fever, flank pain, and leukocyturia in a patient with a history of drug rash, supported by eosinophilic cells on cytospin and a negative bacterial culture, confirms this diagnosis.
